mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the immediate and ultimate corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or equivalent commercial registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the issued certificate by a local notary public; then affix an Apostille from the competent authority designated under the Hague Apostille Convention if the origin jurisdiction is a Convention Contracting State; then obtain certified Chinese translation for filing with SAMR. For jurisdictions that are not Apostille Convention members, replace the Apostille step with authentication by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs followed by consular legalization with the PRC Embassy or Consulate; never chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or comparable corporate registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain from the issuing registry; notarize; take the Hague Apostille route if the origin is a Contracting State; otherwise take the consular legalization route via authentication by the origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then PRC Embassy or Consulate legalization; the two authentication routes are mutually exclusive; then certified Chinese translation for submission with the WFOE incorporation dossier.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney approving establishment of the WFOE and appointing the legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or corporate secretary of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Extract a certified copy of the board resolution or executed power of attorney; notarize the execution; affix an Apostille from the relevant competent authority if the origin jurisdiction is a Hague Convention member; otherwise proceed with authentication by the origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then consular legalization by the PRC Embassy or Consulate. Use only one path per document and never combine Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Articles of Association of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The corporate shareholder authenticated by a local notary public or the corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain a certified copy from the shareholder or registry; notarize by local notary; if the shareholder's jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state, apply for an Apostille from the designated authority; if not, apply for local governmental authentication and then consular legalization by the PRC Embassy or Consulate in that jurisdiction. Prepare certified Chinese translation for SAMR and bank filing; the two authentication pathways are parallel and cannot be sequenced together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the corporate shareholder issued in English
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Depository bank of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Request the bank to issue the reference letter on letterhead with authorized signature; notarize the issuing officer's authority if required; if the bank's jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, attach an Apostille from the relevant competent authority; for non-member states, obtain authentication by the foreign ministry and then consular legalization by the PRC Embassy or Consulate. The apostille and consular routes are mutually exclusive and must not be combined sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, authorized signatories, and material counterparties against: OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; UN Security Council Consolidated List; EU and UK sanctions lists; PRC Ministry of Public Security fugitive and economic crime lists; PRC judicial enforcement databases; and the PBOC/SAMR beneficial owner information disqualification system. Enhanced due diligence applies to all politically exposed persons, family members, and close associates. For ISIC 4690 general re-invoicing and cross-border trade, every underlying counterparty, shipping route, intermediary, and beneficiary bank must be transaction-screened; any sanctions or PEP hit triggers immediate Suspicious Transaction Report to the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center within 24 hours and an automatic freeze of the payment rail. Adverse media and risk-flag reviews must refresh every 90 days and before each Swift_LC, TT_Wire, or XT_Transfer execution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation enterprise name self-declaration system, accessible through SAMR and local market regulation bureaus' government service portals and mirrored by the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Chinese law requires the registered name to be composed of standard Chinese characters in a four-tier structure: administrative division, specific trade name of at least two Chinese characters, industry or business characteristic reflecting trade and re-invoicing, and legal form expressed as Co., Ltd. or Limited Liability Company. Foreign-invested enterprises may use an English name for banking and commercial convenience, but the English name must be a faithful phonetic, semantic, or transliterated equivalent of the Chinese trade name. The Chinese name prevails for all official filings and legal instruments. Names that are homophonically or visually similar to registered names in the same industry are treated as conflicting and are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must obtain and preserve the SAMR rejection notice or the electronic decision code. The applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the same SAMR registry or its superior administrative organ within 60 days of service, or initiate administrative litigation before the competent People's Court within six months. During the appeal, the applicant may simultaneously re-declare a revised name through the same portal. A rejected trade name remains unavailable until the administrative decision is reversed. There is no statutory extension of the 30-day name reservation; if the WFOE incorporation is not completed within that window, the applicant must re-declare the name and may do so immediately as long as no another enterprise has taken it.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or PO Box is not permissible for an ISIC 4690 re-invoicing WFOE. SAMR and local market regulation bureaus require a registered address matching a physical lease and business premises. Tax authorities require an actual operating location for issuing VAT invoices, retaining books, and carrying out routine tax inspections. Banks reject mailbox-only applicants as high-risk and generally refuse to open basic settlement accounts; SAFE will challenge trade remittance substance where the registered office lacks any physical presence. A serviced office with dedicated signage, meeting rooms, lease documents, and full-time staff may satisfy the requirement, but a pure virtual address will be rejected by tax authorities, banks, and SAMR for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Physical inspection likelihood is HIGH, estimated at 65-80% probability during the first 24 months of operation for an ISIC 4690 general re-invoicing WFOE with no warehouse and limited headcount. Unannounced or desk-based inspections may be conducted by SAMR, local tax bureaus, and SAFE. Inspection readiness checklist: posted company sign matching the business license; valid lease contract and property ownership certificate; rent payment vouchers; utility and internet bills; full-time employee presence and labor contracts; original business license; financial records and vouchers; statutory books and board meeting minutes; physical office equipment, servers, and paper archives; and identifiable on-site staff. A virtual office or commercial mailbox will trigger a relocation order, adverse tax risk rating, and bank account freeze.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 1–36 (incorporation), Articles 37–61 (governance and shareholders' resolutions), Articles 62–70 (board of directors), Articles 74–77 (legal representative, executive director and managers), and Articles 88–95 (registered capital and shareholder contribution).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and its local counterpart, the Municipal Market Supervision and Administration Bureau, through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the Integrated Online Government Service Platform (National Portal: www.samr.gov.cn / online registration via 一窗通 equivalent service).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Company (外商投资公司设立登记申请书), together with the Articles of Association, the Joint Venture or Sole Shareholder Decision, the Feasibility Study Report (where required), and the Filing of Foreign Investment Information under the Foreign Investment Law.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No official statutory minimum registered capital for a general trading WFOE under PRC Company Law; however, the registered capital must reasonably match the proposed business scale and operating expenses, and the WFOE must actually contribute the subscribed capital within five years of incorporation. Foreign exchange registration with SAFE requires a minimum operating capital sufficient for projected working capital needs; funds are held in the company's Capital Verification Account (currency settlement account) and are not escrowed by the registry. Paid-up capital schedule and verification require a local bank confirmation letter.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [WFOE] CO., LTD. (PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION) 

WHEREAS, [WFOE] Co., Ltd. (the 'Company') was duly incorporated under the laws of the People's Republic of China on [DATE], with its registered office at [ADDRESS], and authorized share capital of [USD 1,000,000 / RMB equivalent] divided into [100,000,000] ordinary shares of par value [RMB 0.01 each] (the 'Shares');

WHEREAS, the sole shareholder / shareholders of the Company have adopted the Articles of Association and have elected the undersigned individuals to serve as the first board of directors;

WHEREAS, the Directors have received the Company's Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Association, and the shareholders' written resolutions approving the corporate structure and business scope under ISIC 4690 (wholesale trade, re-invoicing, and trading agency services);

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT. The Board hereby ratifies and confirms the initial subscription of the Company's entire registered capital, being [USD 1,000,000 / RMB equivalent], allocated to the sole shareholder as set forth in the Articles of Association. The Board directs the Chairman and the Finance Director to open a designated capital contribution account at a licensed bank in China and to procure deposit of the initial contributed capital in accordance with the agreed contribution schedule. The Board further authorizes the Company to obtain a certificate of capital contribution from the depository bank and to file such certificate with the relevant authority as required by applicable law.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board hereby approves the opening of primary and secondary bank accounts with [BANK NAME], including a basic deposit account, a general deposit account, and a foreign currency settlement account. The Board resolves that the following persons shall be the sole authorized signatories and that any two of the following signatures shall be required for any wire transfer, letter of credit, trade financing, or payment above RMB [X], subject to the payment policy set by the Finance Director. Authorized signatories: [NAME], Director and Legal Representative; [NAME], Finance Director; [NAME], General Manager. The Board further approves execution of corporate banking resolutions, signature cards, and electronic banking agreements in form acceptable to the bank.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The Board hereby ratifies the adoption of the Company's registered office located at [ROOM NO., BUILDING, STREET, DISTRICT, CITY, PROVINCE, CHINA]. The Board confirms that such address is valid for service of process, statutory notices, and official correspondence, and authorizes the General Manager to execute a lease agreement or sublease agreement for the premises for an initial term of not less than 12 months, and to file the address lease, property ownership certificate, or landlord authorization with the Market Supervision Administration and the tax authority.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board hereby appoints [NAME] as Legal Representative (法定代表人) and Chairman of the Board; [NAME] as General Manager (总经理), responsible for daily operations and trade re-invoicing transactions; [NAME] as Finance Director (财务负责人), responsible for books, records, tax filings, and capital control; and [NAME] as Supervisor (监事), responsible for supervision of directors and officers. All officers are authorized to act within their respective scope of duties, and the Legal Representative is specifically authorized to sign government filings, tax registrations, customs declarations (if any), and bank documents.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION. The Board further authorizes the General Manager and Financial Director, jointly acting, to engage certified public accountants, tax advisors, a registered agent, and legal counsel, to execute all forms and instruments required for the company's establishment of social insurance, housing fund, and payroll accounts, and to complete all post-incorporation registrations with the tax authority (Tax Registration), the National Bureau of Statistics, the People's Bank of China, and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE).

The foregoing resolutions were duly adopted by unanimous written consent of the Board of Directors of the Company effective as of [DATE], and shall be filed in the corporate minute book and registered with the appropriate authorities as required by law.

ADOPTED on [DATE] in [CITY], China.

________________________
[NAME], Chairman and Legal Representative

________________________
[NAME], Corporate Secretary / Witness

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Registration Name Reservation and Pre-Approval of Foreign-Invested Enterprise Scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSA) via the National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform (in most cities accessible through the provincial 'Government Service Net' or SAMR National Name Reservation Portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign shareholder must file an online application for name reservation for the proposed WFOE using a Chinese-language company name in the format 'Trade (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.' or equivalent. The application must include the proposed business scope, which cannot simply replicate general wholesale trade; it must be drafted to cover the lawful re-invoicing intermediary activities: '从事国际贸易、转口贸易、贸易经纪与代理、提供供应链管理及相关咨询服务'. Because the scope involves re-invoicing and offshore intermediary trade, the MSA will screen for restricted or prohibited categories under the Foreign Investment Access Negative List (2023 version); if the proposed scope includes any goods regulated under Special Administrative Measures (e.g., certain chemicals, medicines, or strategic materials), the negative-list screening will request additional evidence or a separate applicable license. The applicant must submit the passport or business registration certificate of the sole shareholder, a proof of address of the proposed registered office in China, and a brief explanation of the legal representative's identity. After preliminary name approval (generally valid for 6 months), the applicant must immediately proceed to step 2.
required_dossiers: Application for Name Reservation signed by the foreign investor or its authorized representative
Notarized and apostilled Certificate of Incorporation / Business Registration of the sole foreign shareholder (Chinese translation where required)
Identity certificate of the proposed legal representative (passport or PRC ID where eligible)
Power of attorney appointing a local agent, if applicable
Proposed Articles of Association draft
Foreign investor's bank reference letter (optional but recommended)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name or scope is rejected due to a conflict or negative-list restriction, the applicant may file a written reconsideration with the same MSA within 10 working days, or re-submit with a revised name and a narrower scope. Where the MSA suspects the WFOE intends to engage in a restricted activity, provide an official explanation and remove any restricted phrase from the scope; if the system rejects due to duplicate name, select a new name and re-file immediately at no additional charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application, Articles of Association, and Foreign Investment Filing to MSA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSA) — Investment Promotion / Enterprise Establishment window, online through the national '一手通' one-stop platform or the provincial integrated government service portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the name is reserved, counsel must finalize the Chinese-language Articles of Association containing registered capital, shareholder details, board composition, legal representative, supervisor, registered address, and the re-invoicing business scope. The application must be submitted together with: the signed establishment application form; the name reservation notice; the sole shareholder resolution or foreign parent board resolution authorizing establishment; notarized and legalized/certified shareholder documents; the registered office lease and property ownership certificate of the lessor; the identifications of the legal representative, directors, supervisor, and financial officer; and the foreign investment information filing report under the Foreign Investment Law. If any board member is a foreign national, the passport copy and a notarized specimen signature must be provided. The MSA, in coordination with the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and SAMR's database, will process the application under the 'national treatment plus negative list' system. Because the company is a pure re-invoicing intermediary under ISIC 4690 and does not require a separate operating license, no pre-license is required; however, the application should state that the company will not directly engage in the import/export of physical goods requiring customs permits unless separately approved. The MSA will verify the minimum capital and paid-in schedule; because no statutory minimum applies, the application must specify an amount sufficient to cover at least 12 months of operations and must not state zero capital. After approval, MSA will issue the Business License (营业执照) and assign a unified social credit code.
required_dossiers: Letter of Application for Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Company (signed by the foreign shareholder)
Foreign investor's corporate authorization resolution and certificate of good standing
Notarized and legalized / apostilled shareholder documents (parent company registration certificate)
Chinese-language Articles of Association signed by all shareholders or the sole shareholder
Name reservation notice
Lease agreement for the registered office with valid certificate of property ownership
Copy of proposed legal representative's identity document and specimen signature
Copies of identity documents or passports of all directors, supervisor, and financial officer
Power of attorney for the registered agent and identity copy of agent
Foreign Investment Information Filing Form (采集表格) as required by SAMR/MOFCOM
Undertaking confirming no restricted or prohibited industry activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MSA issues a 'Notice of Correction' or 'Supplement Materials', the applicant has 15 days to cure the deficiencies. For incomplete notarization, obtain a revised apostille from the Chinese consulate or parent company's jurisdiction. For disputes over business scope, submit a revised scope excluding any import/export and wholesale physical-distribution language. If the application is suspended for negative-list review, provide a written explanation that the WFOE acts solely as a re-invoicing intermediary and does not take legal title to goods within the PRC customs territory; if the local MSA remains uncertain, request a pre-ruling from the Foreign Investment Department of the local Commerce Commission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Chop Carving, Tax Registration, Social Insurance, and Post-Incorporation Statutory Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Tax Service Bureau (State Taxation Administration), Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, Housing Fund Management Center, Statistics Bureau, and the MSA-issued integrated 'one-license multi-seal' system (公安备案刻章系统) through the local Public Security Bureau for official company seal engraving.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after receiving the Business License, the applicant must arrange for engraving of the company's official seal (公章), financial seal (财务专用章), legal representative seal (法定代表人章), and invoice seal (发票专用章) at a PSB-approved seal engraving station. Within 30 days, the WFOE must complete tax registration under the unified social credit code, and the tax authorities will automatically activate the tax registration information through the multi-department data sharing. The WFOE must then register for value-added tax (VAT) generally-taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer status; for the re-invoicing intermediary model, the general taxpayer status is recommended if the volume exceeds RMB 5 million per annum, but small-scale status may be initially applicable. The WFOE must also register with the local social insurance agency (pension, medical, unemployment, work-related injury, maternity) and the housing fund center for each local employee. If any foreign employees are seconded from the parent company, the employer must file the foreigner's work permit application before relocation; this step is separately handled by the Entry and Exit Administration and the Human Resources and Social Security Bureau. At the same time, the financial director must open a basic deposit account at a bank and arrange the capital verification or capital contribution confirmation. Under the Foreign Investment Law, the WFOE must file the Foreign Investment Information Report (外商投资信息报告) through the MSA's annual report system and on any changes, including the actual contribution of capital.
required_dossiers: Original Business License and a copy with official seal
Articles of Association and the establishment approval document (if any)
Certificate of official seal engraving from PSB-approved station
Legal representative's identity document and the director's appointment resolution
Office lease agreement and property rights certificate
Incorporation application file and unified social credit code certificate
Shareholder's notarized certificate of incorporation (for foreign-owned corporate shareholder)
Bank account opening information (after step 4)
Payroll and social insurance registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau fails to auto-register the taxpayer due to incomplete information, file a Form 'Tax Registration Supplement' (补充信息采集表) and provide the MSA license and lease. If the social insurance registration triggers a delay, submit a written undertaking to enroll employees within 30 days; do not begin operations without registrations. If the PSB seal engraving system flags the legal representative's name due to unmatched passport, provide a translated passport notarization. If the housing fund office queries the foreign entity's address, present the landlord's certificate and rent payment proof.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Foreign Exchange (SAFE) Registration, and Capital Contribution Remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank authorized to handle foreign exchange settlement (per the local branch), and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the bank's direct-connection system (银行外汇业务直报系统).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The legal representative and financial director must attend a bank interview at the chosen licensed bank with the original Business License, the approved Articles of Association, the company seal set, the board resolution authorizing bank signatories, and the directors' identification documents. The bank will open a basic deposit account (人民币基本存款账户) and a foreign currency capital account (资本项目外汇账户/结算账户). After the bank files the account with the PBOC (People's Bank of China) settlement system, the foreign shareholder must wire the subscribed capital from its overseas bank account to the WFOE's USD or RMB capital account, indicating the purpose as 'Investment Capital'. Once the funds are credited, the bank will issue a bank confirmation (FDI Confirmation / 外方出资确认书) through the SAFE Foreign Investment (FDI) registration system. Under SAFE Circular 16/2013 and the Foreign Investment Law, the WFOE must complete FDI Foreign Exchange Registration (外商投资企业基本信息登记) with the bank (which acts as agent for SAFE) prior to or within 15 working days of receiving the capital. The registered capital may be converted into RMB subject to negative-list screening and used for legitimate operating expenses; for a re-invoicing hub, the funds must not be used for speculation in securities, real estate, or any activity outside the approved business scope. The WFOE must also register the bank account details with the tax authority for refunds and with MSA for the annual reporting of paid-up capital.
required_dossiers: Original Business License and unified social credit code certificate
Company official seal, financial seal, and legal representative seal
First Board Resolution authorizing bank account opening and signatories
Articles of Association (bank version, sometimes required in both Chinese and English)
Passports/IDs of legal representative, directors, and authorized signatories
Residence permit or passport of the legal representative (foreign nationals)
Foreign shareholder's certificate of incorporation and notarized board resolution
FDI Foreign Exchange Registration application form
Office lease agreement
Anti-money laundering questionnaire and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open a basic account due to enhanced AML review (common for non-resident shareholders), provide a notarized source-of-funds letter from the parent company and a written explanation of the re-invoicing transaction flow, together with the parent company's audited financial statements. If SAFE flags the investment as a sensitive sector, submit an explanation referencing the negative list and the WFOE's ancillary services. If the bank reports that the capital account is not activated due to an invalid 'pilgrim' code, request a re-registration amendment through the same bank before the 15-day deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Trade Intermediary Compliance, Customs/Statistics Registration, and Annual Regulatory Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local branch of the General Administration of Customs (GACC) (if direct import/export is later added), the National Bureau of Statistics, the Tax Bureau, and the SAMR enterprise credit portal for annual reports.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Although the WFOE's primary business is offshore re-invoicing and trade intermediation (ISIC 4690), the company must still register the establishment information with the statistics authority and the MSA annual reporting system (市场监管企业年报). If the company later engages in physical cross-border movement of goods, it must apply for Customs Registration of Import/Export Enterprises (海关进出口货物收发货人备案) and, where applicable, the 'Dual Use' or export license related to any controlled products. Because the current scope does not require physical import/export or a pre-establishment license, the WFOE should nevertheless adopt an internal compliance manual compliant with the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law and the Regulations on Foreign Exchange Control to ensure that re-invoicing transactions are supported by underlying contracts, invoices, proof of logistics (e.g., bills of lading from third-party carriers), and evidence of the actual movement of goods from a supplier in one overseas jurisdiction to a buyer in another. The financial officer must maintain a full audit trail showing that the WFOE does not violate the corporate income tax treatment of double non-taxation. Annually, before 30 June, the WFOE must submit the Annual Report on Foreign Investment Information and the annual tax filing through the portal. If the WFOE's annual revenue exceeds thresholds, the tax bureau may require a transfer-pricing documentation file because re-invoicing hubs normally earn a service margin of 3-5% over the cost of goods; the finance director must prepare contemporaneous documentation with pricing policy consistent with the OECD TNMM method to withstand PRC tax audit.
required_dossiers: Business License copy and unified social credit code
FDI foreign exchange registration confirmation
Articles of Association and complete corporate governance documents
List of underlying trade contracts and sample re-invoicing flow diagram
Tax returns and VAT general taxpayer certificate (if applicable)
Transfer pricing documentation policy summary
AML/CTF compliance manual and client due-diligence template
Annual report forms for MSA and foreign investment information filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority challenges re-invoicing margins under the Related Party Transaction Audit, submit a TNMM comparability study or functional analysis; if the annual report is flagged for inconsistency in paid-in capital, provide an updated bank capital verification letter. If the statistics bureau notices that trade volume is reported as zero despite high re-invoicing flows, file a supplemental form indicating 'offshore intermediary service income' and not 'merchandise trade', and correct the trade status code. If a later application to customs is rejected due to the absence of warehousing records, apply as a trading company only and state that goods are shipped directly from supplier to buyer with no physical warehousing in China.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — the WFOE is engaged exclusively in offshore trade intermediation and commercial re-invoicing under ISIC 4690 / NAICS 425120, without physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, warehousing, or any on-site industrial operation. No municipal industrial licensing board approval is required. The competent registration authority for market entry is the local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (SAMR) and the relevant commerce department (MOFCOM foreign investment information reporting system).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — no industrial operating license, manufacturing permit, or wholesale trade license is required under PRC law for a pure re-invoicing intermediary that does not handle physical goods within Chinese territory. The only relevant authorization is the Business License and the automatic tax registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable — Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) and its provincial/municipal Ecology and Environment Bureaus would be the relevant authority if there were an industrial project. Since the WFOE's commercial re-invoicing model involves no plant, no production line, no hazardous chemicals, no wastewater generation, and no warehouse/assembly facility, no EIA registration or approval is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity does not fall under the 'Classified Management List of Environmental Impact Assessment for Construction Projects' (建设项目环境影响评价分类管理名录); no EIA registration form (登记表), EIA report form (报告表), or full EIA report (报告书) is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — the re-invoicing business generates no industrial wastewater, no VOC emissions, no atmospheric pollutants, and no hazardous waste. If the WFOE later opens a representative office or an office-only premises, normal municipal solid waste disposal and office wastewater discharge through the municipal network are the only considerations, and these do not trigger quantitative discharge standards beyond the local sewage discharge permit requirements applicable to ordinary office buildings.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable — no fire safety certification (消防验收备案), structural load inspection, or workplace occupational safety approval is required for a pure office-based re-invoicing business. The WFOE must, however, comply with ordinary office fire safety obligations under the PRC Fire Protection Law by ensuring that the leased office has valid fire inspection or filing records from the landlord, maintaining fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and conducting basic fire safety training. If the company later expands to a physical warehouse or any premises with storage activity (even incidental), Civil Defense and Fire Control authorities will require a Fire Safety Acceptance / Filing (建设工程消防验收备案) and an OHS registration, at which time the licensing and EIA sections become mandatory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China. Online statutory portal: the unified E-Tax platform, also known as the Electronic Tax Bureau, operated by the STA for corporate income tax, value-added tax, invoice issuance and export-tax-refund filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly incorporated WFOE first receives a Uniform Social Credit Code (USCC) from the State Administration for Market Regulation. The USCC constitutes the statutory Tax Identification Number and VAT registration number. Tax registration is completed automatically through data sharing between SAMR and the competent STA tax service office; if automatic activation does not occur, the WFOE's legal representative must complete supplemental tax registration through the E-Tax portal within 30 calendar days after business license issuance, and then register for the export-tax-refund/exemption record in the E-Tax platform if export zero-rating is intended. For a foreign non-resident enterprise with no permanent establishment in China but with Chinese-source income, the payer must withhold and the non-resident must obtain a special non-resident tax record/registration number through the E-Tax portal or the competent local STA office, using its foreign home-country TIN and a China-specific non-resident taxpayer code; no separate physical tax registration certificate is required for pure cross-border income tax withholding.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not offer check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch pass-through elections. The only available elective classification is the VAT general taxpayer election: a taxpayer with annual taxable sales below RMB 5,000,000 may voluntarily register as a VAT general taxpayer if it can satisfy the accounting and invoice-control requirements; a taxpayer above that threshold is compulsorily a VAT general taxpayer. Corporate income tax remains entity-level at 25% for WFOEs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the State Taxation Administration's VAT system; no state-level sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Tax registration is mandatory from business establishment with no turnover-based threshold. The separate VAT general taxpayer registration threshold is annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000 (five million yuan); taxpayers at or below that amount are small-scale taxpayers and generally use simplified VAT collection rates of 3% (or temporary reduced rate of 1% where applicable).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The STA mandates electronic invoicing through the Golden Tax Phase IV system and the Unified Electronic Invoice Service Platform. VAT invoices must be issued from the STA-approved E-Tax/e-invoice module, which transmits invoice data to the STA in real time at issuance. The system applies an STA-generated unique invoice number and electronic anti-fraud signature/digital stamp; invoices that have not been digitally cleared by or reported to the STA are not valid for input-VAT deduction, customs export rebate, or third-party commercial payment. The buyer must authenticate the invoice in the VAT invoice service portal before using it to claim input VAT. Enterprises with annual sales exceeding the local threshold must use the digital e-invoice format; paper or self-developed invoicing is prohibited without a certified VAT tax-control device connected to the STA.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A VAT general taxpayer-exporter may claim China's export zero-rate with input-VAT credit/refund only when the goods are physically exported from Mainland China under a Customs Export Goods Declaration naming the WFOE or the principal as exporter, legal title passes to a non-resident buyer, and the foreign purchaser pays in an approved foreign-currency or RMB settlement. The WFOE must first complete export-tax-refund/exemption record filing with the STA. For a pure re-invoicing hub in which goods do not enter or leave Mainland China customs, the transaction is outside the PRC VAT levy and is not zero-rated export VAT; it is documented as an offshore foreign-to-foreign trade with contracts, transport documents and bank flows that evidence no PRC customs involvement. Qualifying cross-border offshore digital services zero-rating, under Finance and Taxation 2016 No. 36, is not relevant to this goods re-invoicing scope but would require proof that the service is consumed wholly outside China and paid by a non-resident.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration (Customs Declaration for Export Goods) with the electronic release/clearance data matched by China Customs
Bill of Lading or air waybill / multimodal transport document issued to a non-resident buyer and showing shipment from a PRC port or bonded area to a foreign destination
Commercial invoice, packing list, and sale/purchase contracts for the re-invoiced goods
Supplier VAT special invoice plus the STA invoice authentication/verification record, if input-VAT refund is claimed

Bank-issued export foreign-exchange receipt voucher or settlement/collection confirmation, recorded in the SAFE Trade in Goods Foreign Exchange Monitoring System, proving actual repatriation of export proceeds from the non-resident buyer
Completed E-Tax export-tax-refund declaration package (the electronic refund application generated from the official STA export-eligibility data)
Foreign exchange receipt status report showing the export proceeds were received or reported as deferred within the 180-day monitoring period

If the WFOE acts as a re-invoicing intermediary rather than exporter of record, a customs-route proof package consisting of third-party bills of lading, first-sale invoice, second-sale invoice, and non-PRC bank payment routing to prove the goods never entered PRC customs territory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating and VAT refunds are automatically cross-checked by the STA against China Customs release data, enterprise bank account receipts, and the SAFE foreign-exchange monitoring system. If the STA finds that the goods did not physically leave China, the payment was not repatriated within 180 days of export (with no SAFE deferred payment registration), the invoice was declared 0% without a valid customs declaration, or the export documents are false or fabricated, the VAT refund will be clawed back retroactively with delay interest at 0.05% per day, plus an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax involved under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection. If fraudulent export tax refund activity is established, the enterprise also loses export-tax-refund qualification for up to three years and may be subject to criminal liability for fraudulent export tax refund under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. The same clawback period catches unverified invoices and re-invoicing transactions where the underlying goods movement cannot be documented.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC), with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) as the designated foreign-exchange regulatory authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a bifurcated foreign-exchange framework. Current-account transactions, covering merchandise trade, transportation, insurance and profit remittances for foreign-invested enterprises, are administratively convertible provided that the underlying transaction is genuine and supported by invoice, contract, customs records and other documentary evidence. Capital-account transactions, however, remain strictly controlled: inbound foreign direct investment, external loans, guarantees, securities investments and outbound capital disposals require SAFE registration, designated-bank licensing, and post-arrival supervision of use of funds. Export proceeds are subject to repatriation and current-account verification, but the post-2012 reform abolished mandatory surrender, so conversion of export receipts into RMB is optional within an approved current-account foreign-exchange position. Profit remittance by a WFOE is permitted only after the statutory audit is completed, corporate income tax and withholding taxes are paid or cleared, the board resolution on profit distribution is passed, and the bank has reviewed the capital account FDI registration, balance sheet and tax certificate; in practice, mismatched purpose codes, delayed tax payments, or inconsistencies between re-invoice flows and customs declarations can block or delay the remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign-currency proceeds must be repatriated onshore through a PRC designated bank within 180 days from the relevant export customs declaration date; the amount received must be matched with the verified customs value before dispersal. The mandatory conversion ratio is nil after the 2012 SAFE reform, so the WFOE may retain the receipts in a current-account foreign-exchange account or settle them into RMB at its option. Nevertheless, every export receipt must be reconciled with the underlying trade verification data, and any foreign-exchange balance retained without a matching trade file beyond the verification window becomes a regulatory exception requiring SAFE explanation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FDI) and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FDI) and RMB Settlement Account
Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FDI) and Operational Current Account Suite

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury rail. Offshore digital EMIs are legally barred from opening domestic RMB current accounts or FDI capital escrow accounts for a PRC-incorporated WFOE because PBOC banking and SAFE foreign-exchange licensing require the treasury and clearing accounts to sit with a locally licensed bank. An EMI cannot host SAFE-registered capital inflow, cannot issue a Chinese settlement account, and cannot provide auditable trade-verification rails. The only permissible use is as an auxiliary payment collection or settlement channel via an underlying PBOC-licensed payment institution or partner bank for small-ticket or e-commerce payouts; even then, the WFOE should maintain its primary bank accounts at a licensed tier-1 PRC bank to satisfy KYC and regulatory inspections.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory as the default. The legal representative, main beneficial owner and authorized signatories must attend a face-to-face KYC interview at the opening bank branch and complete seal registration and signature specimen in person. Remote consular proxy account opening is not generally accepted; for non-resident directors, banks may accept a notarised power of attorney legalised through the Chinese consulate plus live video verification, but the legal representative or a PRC-based authorised manager must still appear physically to present the company chop, business licence and original identity documents. The WFOE should therefore schedule a physical visit to the bank's regional head office before activation of any transaction line.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership caused by offshore or Hong Kong intermediate holding layers and nominee arrangements, triggering enhanced counterparty due diligence under PBOC anti-money-laundering rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully legalised ownership chain chart from the WFOE through each intermediate entity to the ultimate natural-person UBOs; notarised passports or ID cards of all directors and UBOs; certificate of incorporation, certificate of incumbency and share register for each holding company; declaration identifying no nominee or non-beneficial shareholder; audited financial statements and bank reference letter from the immediate parent; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement for the planned capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade mismatch inherent to re-invoicing: goods move directly from a third-country factory to an overseas buyer while invoicing flows through the PRC WFOE, creating customs, invoice and sanctions-screening gaps.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master supply and distribution contracts; supplier invoice and WFOE re-invoice set showing identical commodity, quantity and prices; bills of lading, air waybills, courier receipts and warehouse records proving physical flow; customs entry and exit declarations from source, transit and destination jurisdictions; transport insurance; incoterms certificate; end-user and end-use certificates for controlled goods; transaction flow map showing party roles in the purchase-payment-resale sequence; counterparty KYC files for downstream buyers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FDI capital injection structured as round-tripping, back-to-back intra-group loans or premature equity distributions; bank sees unusual capital turnover versus working-capital needs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE Foreign-Exchange Business Registration and FDI Information Report; notarised board or shareholder resolution setting the contribution schedule; SWIFT MT103 remittance advices with correct purpose code and currency declaration; PRC CPA capital verification report; audited financial statements of the overseas shareholder proving that the funds are genuine equity surplus; latest WFOE business licence; and a treasury or business plan memorandum explaining the injection relative to the operating cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or watchlist exposure: the re-export chain touches restricted jurisdictions, prohibited end-users or dual-use goods, creating AML/CFT and export-control risk for the bank's correspondent network.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time OFAC, UN, EU and PRC sanctions-screening results for all counterparties, vessels and beneficial cargo owners; adverse-media search documentation; corporate compliance certification and staff AML/CTF training records; export licences or transhipment approvals from relevant authorities; end-user and end-use declarations; transaction monitoring report demonstrating consistent invoice-to-payment matching; and a written undertaking indemnifying the bank against sanctioned-party involvement in the WFOE's global re-invoicing flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The WFOE must complete the initial foreign-investment information report with the market-regulation authority and obtain a Foreign-Exchange Business Registration with SAFE or its designated bank before any cross-border capital remittance. Foreign capital injection should be routed via SWIFT MT103 to the bank-designated FDI capital account, and the payment message must clearly carry the SAFE/balance-of-payments transaction code 6021 or 6022 for direct-investment establishment or capital increase, the creditor and shareholder name, the WFOE enterprise code, and the remittance purpose text equity capital contribution to a PRC wholly foreign-owned enterprise under FDI registration. Upon receipt, the designated bank conducts capital-account confirmation with SAFE's digital system, obtains the company's willing-to-convert statement where applicable, and releases funds into the local RMB account only for permitted purposes. A PRC-licensed CPA subsequently performs capital verification by reconciling the MT103 credit, bank statement, SAFE registration notices, resolution and general ledger; the resulting capital verification report forms the basis for the bank's audit trail and future profit repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary open-account re-invoicing settlements, the WFOE will initiate SWIFT MT103 telegraphic-transfer payments from its RMB or USD operating account through the designated bank, attaching contract, invoice and transport documents for current-account trade verification. For larger or credit-backed deals, the bank will issue irrevocable commercial letters of credit, usually confirmed by a foreign advising bank, to secure the underlying goods payment; alternatively, documentary collections such as documents against payment and documents against acceptance offer a lower-cost route where the bank separately handles negotiable documents. The local clearing side may use CNAPS or RMB cross-border trade settlement rails when invoices are denominated in RMB, or the bank's correspondent network for USD and EUR via New York or London clearing; all disbursements must bear a SAFE current-account purpose code such as goods-trade code 121010 and must be supported by the same trade file as the corresponding import or export declaration. XT_Transfer and similar digital cross-border rails may be used only as supplementary collection or payout interfaces behind a PBOC-licensed payment institution, never as the primary bank clearing certificate for SAFE inspections.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore forward foreign-exchange contracts concluded with a licensed designated bank under SAFE real-trade-background rules; contract amount and maturity must be consistent with the WFOE's current-account receivables or payables and cannot be rolled purely for arbitrage.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible onshore for the PRC entity; they may be transacted only by the offshore parent or group treasury centre with an offshore branch, and the WFOE cannot book or settle NDF cashflows inside China.

Cross-currency swaps permissible only with a PRC-licensed bank for genuine mismatched-currency treasury exposure, limited to the committed trade or loan notional and tenor, with SAFE registration and forward-position reporting where required.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Information Publicity Report (Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June following the close of the fiscal year, with no grace period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the statutory deadline results in inclusion on the Operationally Abnormal List; if the enterprise remains non-compliant for three consecutive years, it is placed on the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List and SAMR may administratively revoke the business license; late filing may also attract local administrative fines, and the legal representative may be subject to public integrity restrictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Information Report (FDI Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and SAMR combined annual reporting portal, with data shared with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) and other regulators
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June following the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the WFOE fails to file or files false information, MOFCOM orders correction within a specified time; if the correction is not made, an administrative fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000 (approximately USD 14,000 to USD 70,000) applies; continued non-compliance may also disrupt foreign-exchange payment and bank settlement transactions for the re-invoicing trade.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement Filing (Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the competent in-charge local tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the year following the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 if the lateness is serious; overdue tax accrues a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax; underreporting or false filing is subject to a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax; prolonged non-filing and registration inactivity may trigger tax-registration revocation and, ultimately, administrative strike-off of the business license by SAMR.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No quantitative balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemption applies. Every Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise limited liability company must appoint an independent licensed PRC CPA firm to audit its annual financial statements under Article 164 of the PRC Company Law and the Foreign Investment Law 2019. The audit must be completed before the annual report and CIT settlement deadlines; an audited financial report is also a condition for the annual FDI information report and for maintenance of foreign-exchange registration applicable to the re-invoicing hub activity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (PRC GAAP / ASBE), issued by the Ministry of Finance and substantially converged with IFRS; a WFOE may elect the simplified Small Enterprise Accounting Standards only if it meets the statutory small-enterprise definition and the local administration accepts that election, but the mandatory audit obligation remains.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of ultimate beneficial ownership and shareholding is delivered through the enterprise annual information report on the SAMR portal; under the Beneficial Owner Information Filing Measures, the WFOE must file beneficial owner information with SAMR at incorporation and within 30 days after any change; any equity transfer, change in registered capital, or change in beneficiary ownership must be amended with SAMR within 30 days, and the shareholder register must be continuously updated.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Senior Management
Register of Charges/Pledges over shares and assets (mortgages/charges)
Minute Book of shareholders' meetings, board meetings, and board of supervisors meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 to USD 2,500 per year for a registered-address or structural agent in a business park or commercial service provider; physical leased office space in tier-1 cities is significantly higher.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 to USD 5,000 per year for a small or mid-sized WFOE conducting general re-invoicing and offshore trade intermediation, subject to transaction volume, cross-border payment rails, and audit complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified High and New Technology Enterprises pay a reduced 15% rate; encouraged industries in the Hainan Free Trade Port and certain Western Region projects also enjoy 15%; Small Low-Profit Enterprises with taxable income not exceeding RMB 3,000,000 and meeting headcount and asset tests enjoy an effective 5% rate; an R&D super deduction of 100% of qualifying research and development expenditure (200% total deductibility) is available; qualified technology transfer income is exempt up to RMB 5,000,000 with 50% inclusion for the excess; certain free-trade-zone and integrated-circuit enterprises may access targeted holidays and reduced rates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return Form A (A class) under the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China, filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal, accompanied by the Quarterly Provisional Payment Return and, where outbound payments are made, the Non-Resident Enterprise Withholding Income Tax Return and related party transaction reporting schedules (G forms).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement filing with quarterly provisional prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional CIT returns are due within 15 calendar days after the close of each quarter (March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31); the annual final corporate income tax return and true-up payment are due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, that is, by May 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales revenue (business income) from the re-invoicing trade of general goods under ISIC 4690 and NAICS 425120, including gross billings to mainland China customers for goods procured from offshore related suppliers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the gross invoice value charged to the mainland buyer. Do not net intercompany procurement or freight cost against sales unless the WFOE acts as a disclosed commission agent. The tax authority may recharacterize a limited-function agency or tolling arrangement as a principal re-invoicing hub if the offshore affiliate lacks economic substance and the WFOE does not bear inventory, credit, or logistics risk; any such recharacterization triggers a 25% CIT assessment on the re-attributed profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs, taxes and surcharges, selling expenses, general and administrative expenses, and financial expenses attributable to the importing, storage, re-invoicing, and distribution activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support every intercompany purchase with valid import customs declarations, freight documents, and trade finance evidence. Payments to offshore affiliates for marketing, management, or procurement services require a benefit test, written contracts, proper Fapiao-compliant invoice trails, and withholding income tax on deemed service fees; unsubstantiated offshore cost pushes are common audit adjustments for re-invoicing hubs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income reconciliation adjustments, including increases for nondeductible expenses, excess entertainment costs, thin-capitalization interest disallowance, and transfer pricing add-backs, and decreases for items such as imputed income reversals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Lines 11 and 12 are the operative bridge between accounting profit and taxable income. The WFOE must disclose any transfer pricing adjustment proposed by the State Taxation Administration and any compensating or offsetting adjustment agreed in a Mutual Agreement Procedure. If the taxpayer fails to prepare Local File or Master File documentation, the tax authority may use indirect profit methods and impose an additional 5% interest surcharge under the special tax adjustment rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income, deemed reduced income, additional deductions, and overseas taxable income from foreign branches or passive investments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE is a Chinese tax resident and must declare worldwide income. Claim the 100% R&D super deduction only for activities physically performed in China with contemporaneous project records. The foreign parent's non-resident status does not reduce the WFOE's resident filing scope; outbound dividends paid by the WFOE are not deducted at the entity level but are subject to withholding at distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year tax losses and computation of current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The general loss carryforward is 5 years; qualified high-tech enterprises and small low-profit enterprises may carry forward 10 years. A re-invoicing intermediary claiming artificial losses created by intercompany pricing below cost or by circular payments will face loss disallowance, upward income adjustment, and penalties; losses from foreign permanent establishments must be ring-fenced separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory tax rate of 25%, computed tax, preferential rate reductions, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% headline rate unless a valid 15% preferential registration is held. Foreign tax credits are available only for qualifying overseas income taxes actually paid and properly evidenced; re-invoicing margins booked in a zero-tax or low-tax offshore jurisdiction without Chinese taxable nexus remain taxable in China and are not eligible for foreign tax credit relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax payable, reduction for quarterly estimated payments already made, and the balance due or refundable for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The balance of tax must be paid by the annual filing deadline. If the WFOE distributes profits after declaring the final annual return, the statutory withholding on the outbound dividend arises at the time of distribution and is payable within 7 days of the payment; any failure to withhold makes the WFOE liable as withholding agent for the uncollected tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Schedules G100000 and related party forms
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory related party transaction annual reporting schedules covering intercompany purchases, sales, services, financing, intangibles, and cost-sharing arrangements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every WFOE with controlled transactions must complete the annual related party disclosure forms even if no transfer pricing adjustment is anticipated. The forms require identification of each offshore related counterparty, the adopted arm's length method, comparable data, and the functional and risk profile. False statements in these schedules can trigger the 50% to 500% civil penalty for tax evasion and criminal exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual or quarterly return triggers a rectification order and a fine of up to RMB 2,000, increased to up to RMB 10,000 for aggravated cases, under Article 62 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law (TCAL). Late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax under Article 32. Fraudulent under-declaration or false return exposure under TCAL Article 63 is a penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded or underpaid amount. Under the 2022 criminal filing standards, evasion of RMB 100,000 or more that also exceeds 10% of the tax due can lead to criminal prosecution; amounts that are especially huge and exceed 30% of tax due face 3 to 7 years' imprisonment. Issuing false special value-added tax invoices in a re-invoicing scheme triggers Criminal Law Article 205, with penalties up to life imprisonment and confiscation of property.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply the bilateral tax treaty reduced rate, the foreign parent must be the beneficial owner of the dividend and hold the WFOE's shares directly with at least a 25% capital interest for a continuous 12-month period if relief to 5% is sought under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA. The WFOE must obtain the foreign tax authority's Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), a beneficial ownership declaration, the certificate of incorporation, copies of the shareholding register, and evidence of substantive decision-making and economic activity by the recipient. The non-resident taxpayer or the WFOE as withholding agent files the Information Reporting Form for Non-Resident Taxpayers Enjoying Tax Treaty Benefits (self-declaration regime) through the Electronic Tax Bureau before or at the time of filing the withholding return. The tax authority may reject relief under the principal purpose test, anti-abuse rules, and SAT Announcement No. 9 (2018) if the recipient is a conduit, lacks functions, staff, premises, or assets, or is not the real economic owner of the dividend. Supporting records must be retained for at least 10 years; if the treaty claim is denied, the under-withheld 10% tax, late surcharge, and penalties are collected from the withholding agent unless the non-resident already paid the tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory withholding is 10%; under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA, interest derived by a financial institution or bank may be reduced to 7%; other bilateral treaties may provide reduced rates. Royalties: statutory withholding is 10%; under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA, royalties covered by the Fifth Protocol (2019) may be reduced to 5%; other treaties provide rates generally between 5% and 10%. All treaty benefits require TRC, beneficial ownership analysis, and substance substantiation; intercompany interest is also limited by the Chinese thin-capitalization debt-to-equity ratio of 2:1 for non-financial enterprises.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation is mandatory when annual related party transactions reach RMB 200,000,000 for tangible asset transfers, RMB 100,000,000 for intangible asset transfers, RMB 100,000,000 for financial asset transfers, or RMB 40,000,000 for other related-party service transactions. Master File obligations arise for qualifying large taxpayers under SAT Announcement No. 42 (2016); Country-by-Country reporting is required when the ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue reaches RMB 5,500,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China enforces economic substance through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) in Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, the beneficial ownership test under SAT Announcement No. 9 (2018), the principal purpose test (PPT) under the OECD Multilateral Instrument, and the special tax investigation rules. A Chinese re-invoicing hub must perform Core Income-Generating Activities within China, including procurement negotiation, logistics coordination, inventory management, credit and market risk assumption, invoicing, treasury, and management decision-making. If the WFOE is a letterbox with no staff, premises, or operational control, the tax authority may disregard the legal form, recharacterize the transaction, attribute profit to the actual functions performed, deny treaty benefits, impose 25% CIT, and assess WHT shortfalls.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and economic substance violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE operates as a pure re-invoicing shell with zero local employees, no business premises, no inventory or credit risk, and no operational decision-making; invoices are routed through the Chinese entity solely to book margin in a tax-favored offshore affiliate while the Chinese entity has no real commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterization under the Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 and Implementation Regulations Articles 120-123; tax authority imposes deemed taxable income at 25%; late payment surcharge at 0.05% per day; civil penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax under TCAL Article 63; blacklisting as a seriously dishonest taxpayer with joint disciplinary restrictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The new PRC Company Law (2023) Article 23 pierces the corporate veil for single-member and group structures; directors who intentionally or grossly negligently cause third-party harm are jointly and severally liable under Article 191. The legal representative and directors face exit bans under TCAL Article 44, asset freezes, and, where the scheme constitutes tax evasion, criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201 with imprisonment up to 7 years and fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and false documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE sells goods at below arm's length prices to its offshore re-invoicing affiliate, pays inflated intercompany management fees or service charges, fails to prepare Local File or Master File despite being above statutory thresholds, and issues false special value-added tax invoices for services never rendered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment under Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 41-48 and SAT Announcement No. 42 (2016); correction of taxable income at the full 25% rate; interest surcharge with up to 5 additional percentage points for lack of contemporaneous documentation; TCAL Article 63 penalty of 50% to 500%; issuance of false special VAT invoices triggers Criminal Law Article 205, punishable by up to life imprisonment and fines or confiscation of property.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or authorize false invoices and fraudulent intercompany contracts may be prosecuted as directly responsible persons for a unit crime, facing personal fines and imprisonment; civil joint liability arises under the Company Law Articles 23 and 191; asset restitution and compensation orders attach to personal estates; exit bans and blacklisting apply to directors and senior officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding tax evasion and sham treaty relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE distributes profits to a letterbox offshore parent in Hong Kong or Singapore without withholding the statutory 10% tax, falsely declares beneficial ownership, presents a fabricated Tax Residency Certificate, and disguises dividends as non-taxable intercompany loans or overcharged royalties to avoid Chinese withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is liable for the unrecovered withholding tax plus late surcharge under TCAL Articles 32 and 69, with a penalty of 50% to 300% of the amount that should have been withheld; false treaty claims are retrospectively denied for up to 5 years under SAT Announcement No. 9 (2018); the 10% statutory WHT and interest are reassessed; in aggravated cases the fraud penalty reaches 50% to 500% under TCAL Article 63.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face piercing liability for corporate tax debts, WHT shortfalls, interest, and penalties; travel bans and property preservation orders are issued; criminal liability arises under Criminal Law Articles 201, 203, and 204 for tax evasion and fraudulent export refund or withholding schemes, with imprisonment ranging beyond 7 years in severe cases; the court may additionally impose fines, disqualify the director from holding office, and order civil restitution to the tax authority.
